59411364.s: Al Jabr is a heritage village and one of the most beautiful old villages south of Al Namas Governorate, still preserving many features of traditional architecture and stone construction. The village reflects the old way of life in the Asir region and attracts heritage lovers and photographers eager to explore the details of authentic mountain architecture that has been preserved to this day.

59411361.s: Namas Archaeological Museum is located in the old quarter, beside a number of old castles and forts with creative designs. The museum holds everything connected to the heritage of the region, including more than 2,000 artefacts.
59411361.b:
Namas Archaeological Museum is located in the old quarter, beside a number of old castles and forts with creative designs. The museum holds everything connected to the heritage of the region, including more than 2,000 artefacts.

The museum has five floors. The first floor holds the agricultural tools the locals used in the past, along with a model of an old well and the traditional methods of drawing water from it. The second floor contains household tools of the past, including appliances such as the telephone, the iron and the television. The third floor houses old weapons such as rifles, spears and daggers of every kind, as well as the heads and horns of hunted ibex and gazelles, and a section of Saudi and foreign banknotes and coins. The fourth and fifth floors hold women's jewellery and adornments for the hands and ears, and all kinds of old women's clothing. The museum also has a corner for stones with inscriptions, the oldest of which dates back to the first century AH, along with many old manuscripts and documents.
59411361.a: Abu Bakr Al Siddiq, Al Sediq, Al Namas

59411357.s: Al Meger Village is in Al Namas Governorate in the Asir region and is known for its location on a high overlook. Its most prominent landmark is Al Meger Palace, a heritage palace that combines Islamic and Andalusian styles and houses a huge collection of old manuscripts and artefacts, including more than a thousand handwritten copies of the Holy Quran, making it one of the region's leading custodians of such treasures. The palace also offers luxurious services and comfortable accommodation for visitors, making a visit a memorable cultural and historical experience for lovers of heritage and traditional architecture.

59411347.s: Al Olayyan is one of the heritage villages of Al Sarh Centre in Al Namas Governorate, Asir region, and dates back about 1,500 years. The village has a museum, a mosque and an ancient fortress, and the museum holds about 3,000 artefacts that reflect the history of the region and the way of life there in the past, making it an important destination for lovers of history and heritage in Asir.

59411311.t: Prince Sultan bin Salman Park in Al Namas
59411311.s: Prince Sultan bin Salman Park in Al Namas Governorate has a large area of green lawns of about 4,500 square metres, along with shaded seating, play areas and several service facilities. The park is a favourite family destination for outings and relaxation in the mild mountain atmosphere of Al Namas, and attracts visitors throughout the year, especially in summer.

59411303.t: Badwah Valley Dam Lake - Al Namas
59411303.s: Badwah Dam was built in 2002 to replenish groundwater wells, provide drinking water for the local people and make use of the water resources of Wadi Badwah. It is a concrete dam, 92 metres long and 30 metres high, with a storage capacity of more than two million cubic metres.
59411303.b:

The Municipal Council of Al Namas Governorate approved a number of proposed projects, including developing Badwah Dam Park, having the municipality equip it and prepare it for investment, and linking it by a dual carriageway from the centre of the governorate to make it a distinctive tourist destination.
59411303.a: Badwah Valley Dam Lake, Al Namas

59411280.t: Tarj Valley Dam Lake - Al Namas
59411280.s: Tarj Valley Dam is one of the largest dams in Al Namas Governorate in the Asir region. It is about 30 metres high and forms a lake behind it that serves as a retreat for local people and visitors. The lake is surrounded by green mountainous terrain that gives it a captivating natural setting, making it a popular destination for outings and photography throughout the year.

59411276.s: Rijal Alma Museum consists of an independent building with a large hall, a smaller hall and a storeroom. The first hall displays documents and coins from Saudi rule and from Gulf, Arab and foreign countries, as well as stamps, inherited old manuscripts and some old books. The second hall displays more than 700 old photographs, framed and on show, along with local heritage pieces including utensils, lanterns and old weapons.

59411266.s: Rijal Alma Heritage Village is a heritage village in Rijal Alma Governorate in the Asir region of south-western Saudi Arabia, about 52 km west of the city of Abha. It is more than 900 years old. The village was an important point linking travellers from Yemen and the Levant on their way through Makkah and Madinah, which made it a major trading centre. The village consists of about 60 buildings made of natural stone, mud and timber, and the site includes a museum established by the villagers.

59411110.s: The Heritage Village is a showcase of the folk heritage of the Jazan region. It holds the traditional tools used in the mountain, marine and coastal environments, including clothing, ploughing tools, old weapons and the vessels used in each environment. It also features the talents and creativity of local people in painting and arrangement, the aromatic plants the region is rich in, distinctive products of productive families, and the blue tea produced in the Jazan region.

59411108.s: Jazan Heritage Castle, also called Al Dosariyah Castle, is an archaeological fortress standing on a hill overlooking the Red Sea in the centre of Jazan in southern Saudi Arabia. It dates back to the Ottoman era, when it served as the seat of the Turkish governor. It stands about 150 metres above sea level, is square in shape with a total area of about 900 square metres, and is reinforced by four massive towers. The Ministry of Tourism began restoring and restructuring the castle in January 2012 in three phases.
59411108.b: Jazan Heritage Castle, also called Al Dosariyah Castle, is an archaeological fortress standing on a hill overlooking the Red Sea in the centre of Jazan in southern Saudi Arabia. The Ministry of Tourism began restoring and restructuring the castle in January 2012 in three phases. The first phase was clearing the rubble, the second was installing electricity and developing the area around the castle, and the third and final phase was building the museum inside the castle.

59411099.s: Habar Island, or Ahbar Island, is one of the islands in the Red Sea, also known as Dhu Al Rakah Island. It lies 15 km off the coast of Jazan Governorate in south-western Saudi Arabia and is an ideal retreat for tourists looking to enjoy sandy beaches, turquoise sea, green spaces, promenades, cafes, seafood restaurants and a wide range of water activities. The island also attracts many divers and anglers, and nature lovers can discover many species of rare and migratory birds. The island covers an area of about 1.1 square km.
59411099.b:
Habar Island, or Ahbar Island, is one of the islands in the Red Sea, also known as Dhu Al Rakah Island. It lies 15 km off the coast of Jazan Governorate in south-western Saudi Arabia and is an ideal retreat for tourists looking to enjoy sandy beaches, turquoise sea, green spaces, promenades, cafes, seafood restaurants and a wide range of water activities. The island also attracts many divers and anglers, and nature lovers can discover many species of rare and migratory birds. The island covers an area of about 1.1 square km.

The island also has many kinds of hot springs, to which tourists come from all over the world for therapeutic tourism. It has a variety of coral reefs, as it faces the Red Sea, which is known for its distinctive coral reefs and its mild climate throughout the year. The island has been developed to meet all visitors' needs and is equipped with many seating areas and boat piers, so tourists can hire a boat to reach all the places and beaches on the island.

59408447.s: The Uthman ibn Affan Farm and Well is one of the old historical and archaeological landmarks of Madinah, in the north-west of the city, about five kilometres from the Prophet's Mosque, at the bottom of the blessed valley known as Wadi Al Aqiq, near the Al Sayl complex. It is a very old farm containing the well that Uthman ibn Affan bought as a donation for those in need. The whole farm has been cared for throughout the ages and planted with various crops such as date palms, along with many nurseries for vegetables and fruit spread across the farm.
59408447.b: The Uthman ibn Affan Farm and Well is one of the old historical and archaeological landmarks of Madinah, in the north-west of the city, about five kilometres from the Prophet's Mosque, at the bottom of the blessed valley known as Wadi Al Aqiq, near the Al Sayl complex. It is a very old farm containing the well that Uthman ibn Affan bought as a donation for those in need. The whole farm has been cared for throughout the ages and planted with various crops such as date palms, along with many nurseries for vegetables and fruit spread across the farm. The farm became the first waqf (endowment) in the history of Islam.

59408433.s: One of the most important landmarks visited by those coming to Madinah, it is a group of small mosques. There are in fact six rather than seven, but it became known by this name because some people include the Qiblatayn Mosque among them, since whoever visits them also visits that mosque on the same trip, making seven.

59408432.s: Bir Athq is located west of Quba Mosque, slightly to the south. The homes of Banu Amr ibn Awf of the Aws tribe once stood on the site, and from then on the well became blessed. It is one of the Prophetic wells of Madinah, documented by the people of Madinah and by historians, and it is known to this day.

59408388.s: The Western Jamma is Jamma Al Aqir (also known as Jamma Al Aqil), one of the three jammas overlooking Wadi Al Aqiq west of Madinah. It lies to the north-west of Jamma Tadhari and Jamma Umm Khalid and is the farthest of them from the city, about nine kilometres from the Prophet's Mosque, and it is also the largest and most massive of the jammas. Several palaces were once built at its foot along Wadi Al Aqiq, the most famous being the palace of Jafar ibn Sulayman.

59408370.s: Hisn Bani Waqif, or Utum Bani Waqif, lies about 500 metres south-east of Quba Mosque. It is one of the historical landmarks and monuments of Madinah and is only four kilometres from the Prophet's Mosque. Researcher Muhammad Ghali Al Tarjami stated that the Banu Waqif, after whom the fort is named, were from the Aws, one of the tribes of the Ansar who supported the Messenger (peace be upon him), noting that the Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed in their fort, which lies south of Quba Mosque.

59408367.s: The Prophet's Mosque is the second holiest mosque for Muslims after the Grand Mosque (Masjid al-Haram) in Makkah, and lies in the heart of Madinah. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) built it himself in the year of the Hijra (622 CE) as soon as he arrived in Madinah. It began as a simple mosque of mud and palm trunks, and was then expanded repeatedly through the ages, from the Rightly Guided Caliphs through the Umayyad, Abbasid and Ottoman eras up to the Saudi era, which saw its largest expansions, bringing its current area to more than 400,000 square metres and accommodating more than a million worshippers.
59408367.b: The Prophet's Mosque is the second holiest mosque for Muslims after the Grand Mosque (Masjid al-Haram) in Makkah, and lies in the heart of Madinah. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) built it himself in the year of the Hijra (622 CE) as soon as he arrived in Madinah. It began as a simple mosque of mud and palm trunks, and was then expanded repeatedly through the ages, from the Rightly Guided Caliphs through the Umayyad, Abbasid and Ottoman eras up to the Saudi era, which saw its largest expansions, bringing its current area to more than 400,000 square metres and accommodating more than a million worshippers. The mosque contains the Rawdah, the area between the Prophet's (peace be upon him) pulpit and his noble chamber, which he described as "a garden from the gardens of Paradise". The Prophet's Chamber holds the grave of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his two companions Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them). The mosque is known for its famous Green Dome, its ten minarets, its wide gates, its domes and its retractable umbrellas, and it is a main destination for every pilgrim, Umrah visitor and visitor to Madinah throughout the year.

59408363.s: Assalam Museum is one of the most prominent Islamic places you can visit, where you can learn a great deal about the religion and the history of Islam in general, and the history of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in particular. The museum is located near the Haram at the Prophet's Mosque, and is a place you should not miss while in Madinah. It has a very well-presented exhibition that lets you learn about the life of the Messenger of Allah from his birth, through his journey spreading Islam, to his death. Visit it with your family and children or friends, and enrich your religious knowledge.

59408301.s: Al Madinah Museum is a government museum that showcases the heritage and history of Madinah. It holds various archaeological collections, visual exhibition halls and rare photographs related to Madinah, and displays about 2,000 rare artefacts that embody the heritage and culture of the city and document its natural landscapes, its people and how it took shape over the years. One of the most interesting parts of the museum tour is the evolution of the Prophet's Mosque from a house and courtyard into the vast complex it is today.
